title: Rename contract to solution in the backend
request: Users should meet a 'solution' they draft and refine, not a 'contract'. The owner chose to rename it in the UI and in the backend, without breaking anything written before.
spec: studio/solution.py with the Solution model; the project key solution; routes /solution* with /contract* kept as hidden aliases; the gate solution and the policy require_solution_signoff, with old names mapped. Done when the rename, studio and graph tests pass and an old project.json with a contract key opens and is rewritten.
plan: Ask the owner how far the rename should go (only the draft step, the whole UI, or UI and backend); the owner chose UI and backend.
Move studio/contract.py to studio/solution.py and keep contract.py as a thin re-export.
Migrate old project.json files on read in ProjectStore (contract to solution, old gate and policy names).
In the graph, name WF-01 'Solution draft', the gate 'solution', the policy require_solution_signoff, and map the old move, gate and policy names.
Add /solution and /solution/proposal routes, keep /contract as aliases hidden from the schema; update engine, export, SFT and tests; add a migration test.
Protect research wording that is part of immutable records.

decisions.decision: Old names keep working for one release: hidden route aliases, LEGACY_MOVES, LEGACY_GATES, LEGACY_POLICY, a migrating store.
decisions.why: Existing projects, scripts and Chat UI setups must not break because a word changed.

decisions.decision: Research records keep their wording: rule DCLAB-R01 'prediction contract', campaign results, the SFT corpus, evidence.
decisions.why: Those are immutable or generated records; renaming them would rewrite history.

decisions.decision: 'Contract' as a column name in the Telco data and as a research field in tests stays.
decisions.why: It is the dataset's own column, not the product's object.

change: studio/solution.py (Solution, propose) with studio/contract.py as a shim; the project field solution with migration on read; graph WF-01 'Solution draft', gate solution, policy require_solution_signoff with legacy maps; /solution routes with hidden /contract aliases; engine, export, SFT and tests updated; tests/test_solution_rename.py.

findings.defect: The earlier UI at /classic would have broken after the backend rename.
findings.scenario: The old UI's scripts read p.contract from the project; after the store migrated files to the solution key, the old Solution view would have shown nothing.
findings.cause: The rename covered the new frontend and the backend but the old frontend reads the same API.
findings.fix: Rename the field in the old UI's scripts too, so /classic keeps working until it is removed.
findings.impact: Anyone still on /classic, at the time the only UI that could start research campaigns, would have opened a project and found an empty Solution view, as if the signed-off contract were gone, though it was stored under its new key.
findings.open: The fix kept /classic working only until 8.3 removed it. The hidden /contract aliases were promised for one release and need their own removal.

outcome: Done: the backend speaks of the solution everywhere; old project files, routes, moves, gates and policies still work; make rd-check passed (137 tests).
lessons: A rename that touches stored data needs a migration on read and aliases for every external name, tested with an old file.
risks: Old project.json files with a contract key open with no solution after the rename unless the store migrates them on read.
Scripts, Chat UI setups and MCP configs that use /contract routes, the set_contract move, the contract gate or the old policy switch break.
A blanket search-and-replace rewrites immutable research records, rule DCLAB-R01's 'prediction contract' and the Telco dataset's own Contract column.
The old UI at /classic reads the same API and silently loses the renamed field.
SFT examples and other generated files go stale unless they are rebuilt after the rename.
